approved: Emergency Response Fund Amendment (Disaster Ready Fund) Bill 2022

The majority voted in favour of *disagreeing* with an [amendment](https://parlinfo.aph.gov.au/parlInfo/search/display/display.w3p;db=CHAMBER;id=chamber%2Fvotes%2F19a53668-c83d-4ab5-b553-9c63c4331d85%2F0045;query=Id%3A%22chamber%2Fvotes%2F19a53668-c83d-4ab5-b553-9c63c4331d85%2F0000%22), which means it was unsuccessful. Note that this is an amendment to a [second reading](https://peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/) motion, which means that it would have no legal force even if it had succeeded. Instead, these types of motions are symbolic and represent the will of the House majority. Note also that "*to give a bill a second reading*" is parliamentary jargon for agreeing with its main idea. ### Motion text > *That all words after “That” be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *“whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House:* > > *(1) expresses concern that the Government is seeking to remove an additional source of funding for natural disaster recovery at the very moment when many communities across south-east Australia are facing many months of work to clean up after devastating floods; and* > > *(2) notes the Government has not yet identified what disaster mitigation actually encompasses”*
Emergency Response Fund Amendment (Disaster Ready Fund) Bill 2022 - in Committee - No investment in fossil fuels

The bill transforms the former government's $4.8 billion Emergency Response Fund, which spent nothing on mitigation or recovery over three years, into the Disaster Ready Fund providing up to $200 million annually for resilience and risk reduction projects. The government also announced $150 million for recovery in the Northern Rivers region and the establishment of the National Emergency Management Agency to administer disaster-related functions.
